item.text:
Turn complete. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

This turn I built the independent invariant harness I'd flagged as remaining work, and it produced a clean negative result.

`work/zz_audit_invariants_test.go` (gated behind `-tags auditdiag`, so it doesn't touch the captured suite) does not reuse the repo's own assertions. It builds a 5-node in-memory cluster, runs a continuous writer that records every command whose `Apply().Error()` returns nil, then over 4 rounds isolates the current leader at the transport level, lets a new leader emerge, and heals. Afterwards it requires (a) all five FSMs to hold an identical applied-command sequence and (b) every acked command to be present.

```
go test -tags auditdiag -v -count=10 -run '^TestAuditRandomPartitionInvariants$' .
--- PASS ×10   ok  github.com/hashicorp/raft
# per run: rounds=4, acked ≈680–800, missing=0, all 5 FSMs identical
```

Across 10 runs — 40 partition rounds and roughly 7000 acked commands — there was no divergence and no loss of any acked command. That is a strong independent negative for the leader-failover, log-truncation, and rejoin paths under randomized partitions.

I also confirmed hygiene: `go vet .` passes with no tags (the diagnostic files are excluded from the default build), and the tagged reproductions remain runnable.

Status after this turn:

- Finding 1 (confirmed, low severity): `testing.go`'s `EnsureSamePeers` freezes its reference peer set, making `TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3` fail ~15–30% on a healthy cluster; reproduced and controlled.
- No consensus-level defect: source review of every critical path, the full suite, a 40-test core-consensus batch (5× each), and now an independent randomized partition harness all come up clean.
- Honest residual uncertainty: whether Finding 1 is the injected mutation or a latent upstream flake, since the module cache's provenance can't be trusted offline.

If the runner continues, the remaining useful directions are narrower: extend the harness to multi-node partitions and mixed protocol versions, or attempt to obtain a trustworthy upstream reference for a byte-level diff (currently blocked by no network).
